To determine how the rate of smoking has changed over time among Americans, we can consider historical data and public health trends. Over the past several decades, smoking rates in the United States have generally declined. This decline is attributed to increased awareness of the health risks associated with smoking, public health campaigns, higher taxes on tobacco products, and restrictions on smoking in public places. Therefore, the rate of smoking has not stayed flat or increased; rather, it has decreased over time.
